case.case_title: Bandara and Another v. Premachandra, Secretary, Ministry of Lands, Irrigation and Mahaweli Development and Others
case.source_citation: Supreme Court of Sri Lanka, S.C. Application No. 213/93, decided on 8th, 9th and 23rd June 1993

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioners' purported dismissal for participation in trade union activities violated their fundamental right to freedom of association under Article 14(1)(c).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioners argued that their dismissal was due to their participation in trade union activities, which is protected under Article 14(1)(c), and that their rights were infringed.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents contended that the dismissal was due to misconduct (submission of false sick notes) and that the petitioners were not entitled to protection under Article 14(1)(c).
key_facts: Petitioners were appointed on probation to a surveying degree course and became members of a trade union.
They participated in a work-to-rule campaign and submitted sick notes for absence.
The 2nd respondent informed them their services were terminated due to participation in trade union activity.
Petitioners were not dismissed for misconduct but for trade union participation.
The court found the petitioners' conduct tainted with misconduct but relief was granted under Article 12, not Article 14.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 14(1)(c) protects the right to form and join associations, including trade unions, and to participate in their lawful activities. The right is not limited to initial membership but extends to continuing participation.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court acknowledged that the petitioners were dismissed due to their trade union participation, not misconduct. However, since their conduct involved misconduct (submission of false sick notes), the court refrained from granting relief under Article 14(1)(c) and (d), instead granting relief under Article 12(1).
principles_established: Freedom of association includes the right to participate in lawful trade union activities.
Misconduct can taint trade union activities and affect protection under Article 14.
Relief under Article 14 is not automatic if misconduct is involved.

outcome.holding: The court did not grant relief under Article 14(1)(c) because the petitioners' conduct was tainted with misconduct, but recognized the right to freedom of association as including lawful trade union activities.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: The petitioners' dismissal was directly linked to their participation in trade union activities, which falls under the protection of freedom of association in Article 14(1)(c). The court engaged with this clause to assess the scope of protection and its limits when misconduct is involved.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The purported dismissal of the Petitioners was on account of their participation in trade union action, and not on account of any misconduct or considerations therewith. Article 14(1)(c) is of general application to all forms of associations, including trade unions; and not only to the initial act of forming or joining an association, but to continuing membership and participation in the lawful activities of the association.
